question:
Find the volume (in cm³) of a sphere having a diameter of 22 cm, giving your answer correct to two places of decimal.

Take π = (22)/(7).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius of the sphere (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 22 ÷ 2 = 11 cm

Volume = (4/3) × π × r³

Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 11³ = (88 × 1331) ÷ 21

Volume = 117128 ÷ 21 = 5577.5238...

Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 5577.52 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5577.52 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Where r is the radius of the sphere.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 22 ÷ 2 = 11 cm

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (11)³

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 1331

⇒ Volume = (88 × 1331) ÷ 21

⇒ Volume = 117128 ÷ 21

⇒ Volume ≈ 5577.5238 cm³

⇒ Volume correct to two decimal places = 5577.52 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5577.52 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is given by the formula 4 × π × r².

Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a sphere. Its volume is given by (2/3) × π × r³.

Total Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The total surface area of a hemisphere includes the curved surface and the flat circular base, given by 3 × π × r².
